scenes.title: Problem
scenes.narration: Someone sends you a screenshot: “Where do I press?” On a call, neither of you can see what the other means. ShowMe sends back one clear visual next step. This example uses made-up billing details.

scenes.title: Privacy review
scenes.narration: I add the screenshot and the goal: cancel my subscription. The browser detects structured details such as emails and card numbers. Detection is partial, so I review the picture and brush out this name myself. Only after I continue does the reviewed, redacted image go to ShowMe and Meta.

scenes.title: Meta models
scenes.narration: Muse Spark identifies the next control. SAM can refine the highlight when its bounding box agrees with Spark’s and contains Spark’s point. Otherwise, ShowMe keeps the box. Refinement never changes the click point.

scenes.title: Recipient handoff
scenes.narration: I review the image again, consent to sharing, and create an expiring link. On the iPhone, the recipient gets one instruction and a highlight. They use it to find the matching control on the original example. This is a picture, not remote control, and no subscription is changed. Another step needs another screenshot. The link expires after seven days.

scenes.title: Engineering
scenes.narration: Here is the engineering I built during the hackathon. The browser re-encodes the reviewed image, and the API client requires that redaction result. Tests inspect the uploaded payload. The SAM agreement gate rejects inconsistent refinement.

scenes.title: Recorded evidence
scenes.narration: On prompt version three, the click point landed inside the labelled target in 89.9 percent of 1,172 held-out grounding examples. When the target was absent, it said “not visible” in 151 of 200 probes, 75.5 percent. Most of the rest still got a highlight, and we publish those failures.

scenes.title: Close
scenes.narration: ShowMe is for the person who receives the screenshot: review locally, send one clear step, and let the recipient stay in control. Try the live app and inspect the code.
